challenges.name: zero-values-shadowing-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: shadowing, zero values and integer division
challenges.description: Run a shadowed counter in your head, then decide which zero values and divisions behave the way their authors expected.

questions.explanation: count := count + 1 inside the if declares a NEW variable named count in the if block. On the right-hand side, count still means the outer variable (the new one only exists after the statement), so the inner count is 0 + 1 = 1 both times, and it disappears at the closing brace. The outer count is never assigned, so the last line prints 0: the output is 1 1 0. It compiles because the inner count is used by fmt.Print. "1 2 2" is what count = count + 1 (or count++) would print. "1 2 0" would need the inner variable to survive between iterations, but each pass through the block starts a fresh scope.

options.text: It does not compile: count is declared twice

questions.question: Parcel is a struct with a string field ID. Which of these statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Reading a missing key from a map gives the value type's zero value, and that works even on a nil map: var stock map[string]int; stock["SP-1021"] is 0 (only WRITING to a nil map panics). 3 / 4 * 100 is integer arithmetic from left to right: 3 / 4 is 0, so the result is 0. Dividing an int by a variable that is 0 compiles and panics at run time with "integer divide by zero" (10 / 0 with a constant 0 is rejected by the compiler instead). A nil *Parcel has no Parcel to read, so p.ID panics with "invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference" - it does not give the zero string. And Go never converts between numeric types for you: cash / n with an int64 and an int is the compile error "invalid operation: cash / n (mismatched types int64 and int)"; write cash / int64(n).

options.text: var stock map[string]int, then fmt.Println(stock["SP-1021"]) prints 0
var p *Parcel, then fmt.Println(p.ID) prints an empty line
var cash int64 = 439000; n := 3; fmt.Println(cash / n) prints 146333
zero := 0; fmt.Println(10 / zero) compiles, then panics at run time with "integer divide by zero"

challenges.name: driver-cod-summary
challenges.title: Write the driver's end-of-day COD summary
challenges.description: Every evening a Saigon Parcel driver hands in the cash collected on delivery (COD). Write summarize and successRate for the end-of-day report: count the parcels and the delivered ones, add up the cash of delivered parcels only, find the delivered parcel with the largest COD, and compute the success rate as a percentage. Watch the zero values: a parcel paid online has COD 0, a day can have no deliveries, and a day can have no parcels at all. The test runner reads one parcel per line and prints the report.

tests.name: Two of three parcels delivered
tests.input:
SP-2001 350000 delivered
SP-2002 120000 failed
SP-2003 89000 delivered
tests.expected:
parcels: 3
delivered: 2 (66.7%)
cash: 439000 VND
largest: SP-2001 350000 VND

tests.name: Failed and returned parcels bring no cash; a tie keeps the first parcel
tests.input:

SP-2102 90000 returned
SP-2103 150000 delivered
SP-2104 500000 failed
tests.expected:
parcels: 4
delivered: 2 (50.0%)
cash: 300000 VND
largest: SP-2101 150000 VND

tests.name: Nothing delivered: the rate is 0.0% and there is no largest parcel
tests.expected:

delivered: 0 (0.0%)
cash: 0 VND
